**Best fit: [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2).** Its 2,600 W AC output is enough for a typical single-burner induction cooktop rated up to 1,800 W, with some headroom; its 2,073.6 Wh battery also gives it more cooking capacity than a small station. ([Specs and cooking estimates](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop))

It should also run an electric kettle **if the kettle’s wattage is below 2,600 W**—check its label, and don’t run other high-power appliances at the same time. As a rough guide, boiling a litre uses about 90–110 Wh, while an induction cooktop on high drains the battery much faster. ([Source](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop))
